sources.news_title: Requires Response From Nvidia
sources.text:
USA's finansminister, Scott Bessent, vil have svar på, hvorvidt Nvidia bevidst har tilladt, at det amerikanske selskabs mest avancerede chips til kunstig intelligens er havnet i Kina.
Det siger han søndag i Fox News-udsendelsen 'Sunday Morning Futures' tre dage efter, at Jensen Huang fratrådte sin stilling som topchef for Nvidia.
Helt konkret ønsker finansministeren at få klarlagt, hvorvidt Nvidia har gjort brug af skuffeselskaber for at omgå amerikanske eksportrestriktioner og sælge selskabets mest avancerede chips til Kina.
USA har i et forsøg på at bevare sit forspring i kapløbet om kunstig intelligens indført et forbud mod salg af de mest avancerede AI-chips til Kina.
I slutningen af 2025 gav USA's præsident, Donald Trump, dog tilladelse til, at Nvidia må sælge selskabets H200-chips til Kina.
- Intet, der er mere avanceret end H200-chips, må sælges til kineserne, siger Bessent søndag og tilføjer:
- Det vigtigste her er at undersøge, om Nvidia havde en kultur, hvor man overholdt de amerikanske eksportrestriktioner.
Finansministeren henviser til selskaber med forbindelser til selskabet Megaspeed, der ligger i Singapore, og som Jensen Huangs formodede elskerinde Alice Huang arbejdede for.
- Og hvem vidste hvad? For jeg mener, at disse skuffeselskaber var åbenlyse. De var under efterforskning. Og brugte Nvidia dem som omvej til at sælge chips til kineserne?
Om Alice Huang siger Bessent:
- Det er ligegyldigt for mig, om hun er spion eller ej. Jensens personlige svagheder er hans egne.
Bessent kræver, at Nvidia inden for ti dage kommer med svar på spørgsmålene og fremlægger resultaterne af selskabets interne undersøgelse af Jensen Huangs adfærd.
USA mistænker Megaspeed for at have hjulpet kinesiske virksomheder med at omgå amerikanske eksportrestriktioner ved at købe chips fra Nvidia til selskabets datacentre i Sydøstasien og derefter sende dem videre til Kina.
Det amerikanske justitsministerium er i gang med en strafferetlig efterforskning af sagen.
Nvidia meddelte i slutningen af oktober, at selskabet allerede sidste år undersøgte sagen, og tilbageviste beskyldningerne.
RITZAU/AFP

sources.news_title: Bessent: Nvidia should 'go outside the company' for next CEO
sources.text:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday Nvidia’s board shouldn’t prioritize an internal replacement for former CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down after admitting to having an affair with an employee and alleged Chinese spy last Sunday.
“As the board conducts a search for a new leader… they need to go outside the company,” he said while speaking with Larry Kudlow on Sunday Morning Features. “That, just, what was going on, inside the company, they need a dramatic shake-up. Because, Larry, I can tell you, that Nvidia is a wonderful company, Jensen Huang is a wonderful innovator, but that does not abrogate their duties of compliance.”

sources.news_title: US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
sources.text:
US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
Scott Bessent gives Nvidia’s board 10 days to show the company’s compliance with US export controls.
United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for an outsider to take the helm at Nvidia, the California-based technology giant that has faced scandal over its former chief executive, Jensen Huang.
Speaking on Fox News’s Sunday Morning Futures programme, Bessent said the company should look beyond its own ranks for Huang’s successor.
“This makes me think that, as the board conducts a search for a new leader, that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent told Fox News. “Just [with] what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shake-up.”
Bessent’s comments come three days after Huang stepped down on Thursday, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman US officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia plays a leading role in producing chips and other computing components for artificial intelligence (AI).
As a result, the company has been at the centre of a technology race between the US and China, with the two superpowers competing for dominance in the growing AI sector.
Huang was long a key figure at Nvidia, as one of the company’s cofounders. Since 2025, he has also cultivated a close relationship with the second administration of US President Donald Trump.
In August 2025, for instance, Huang successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen restrictions on the sale of H20 microchips to China, in exchange for the US government taking 15 percent of the sales.
But in late October, The New York Times revealed Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s clients.
The report cited unnamed US intelligence agents who believed Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to help the country’s firms navigate US chip restrictions.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Beijing has denied the allegations, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.
Alice Huang has not publicly commented on the claims. She reportedly left Megaspeed in 2025.
Tightening chip controls
For his part, Jensen Huang had long maintained that wider access to US technology would help Washington preserve its edge in the global AI race.
Bessent, however, questioned whether Nvidia had turned a blind eye to potentially illicit chip sales to bolster its financial results.
In Sunday’s television appearance, Bessent suggested a 10-day deadline for the company to show its compliance with US export controls.
“I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel,” Bessent said.
“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?”
The controversy has encouraged a bipartisan push in Congress to tighten controls on US chip exports to China.
Lawmakers, including Republican Senator Jim Banks and Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, have sought to use the annual end-of-year defence bill to close loopholes that Chinese companies can exploit to obtain advanced US-designed semiconductors.
But Bessent questioned the need for new laws, telling Fox News host Larry Kudlow that Washington’s existing export controls were sufficient but needed better enforcement.
“I don’t think we need the legislation,” he said. “We have all the rules we need; we just need them enforced.”
A new leader for Nvidia?
Since Huang’s departure, rumours have swirled about who might replace him at Nvidia’s helm.
The company’s board has floated Rene Haas, the chief executive of the semiconductor firm Arm Holdings, as a possible successor to Huang, according to the Financial Times.
Haas is no stranger to Nvidia, having spent several years at the company before joining the British chip designer.
Trump, meanwhile, has named former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as a potential candidate.
In a post on Truth Social on Thursday, Trump praised Huang’s work at Nvidia and said Cook was an ideal candidate to replace him.
“A Legend replaces a Legend,” Trump wrote.
But the Financial Times has suggested Huang may seek to return to his top-level post. In a report on Sunday, the publication said unnamed allies of his are rallying Silicon Valley executives to support his return to the company.
“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” one source told the Financial Times.
Currently, chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading Nvidia on an interim basis.

sources.news_title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Demands ‘Dramatic Shakeup’ At Nvidia, Calls For Outside CEO – 100PercentFedUp.com – by Jack
sources.text:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent just put Nvidia’s board on notice: replacing Jensen Huang is not enough.
In a Sunday interview, President Trump’s Treasury secretary said the AI-chip giant needs a “dramatic shakeup” and should look outside the company for its next CEO.
His warning went well beyond one executive. Bessent questioned whether Nvidia had developed a culture that tolerated sales designed to get advanced chips into Chinese hands despite American export controls.
Bessent also pointed straight back at the Commerce Department when pressed about why the restrictions were not enforced sooner.
Bessent is still backing the bus over Lutnick: "I'll leave the internal workings of the Commerce Department to the Commerce Department" pic.twitter.com/msmr7XoFIJ
— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 15, 2026
This is now a fight over more than palace intrigue in Washington or Silicon Valley.
Nvidia’s chips sit at the center of the global AI race. If shell companies were used to route restricted technology toward China, the damage reaches American national security, investor confidence, and the integrity of the export-control system.
Axios reports that Bessent wants answers from Nvidia’s board and outside counsel within 10 days. He also asked whether seemingly illicit sales were pushed to inflate revenue and earnings, while Nvidia had not immediately responded to the outlet’s request for comment.
That is an explosive question from a sitting Treasury secretary. It is still a question, however, not a formal finding that Nvidia falsified its financial results.
The timing could hardly be worse for the company. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results Tuesday, giving Kress her first major public test as acting CEO while shareholders are already trying to measure the damage from Huang’s departure.
The report also places the fight inside President Trump’s Cabinet. Bessent has pressed for tougher enforcement, while questions remain about why the Commerce Department did not act sooner against companies suspected of serving as Chinese fronts.
Nvidia’s board is now facing pressure from investors, regulators, and competing power centers inside the administration at the same time.
Bessent’s comparison with a regulated bank made his point even sharper: a compliance breakdown of this scale would not be treated as a one-man problem.
🚨 JUST IN: Treasury Sec. Scott Bessent just said if a BANK did what Nvidia did, MULTIPLE executives would be removed from the company immediately
Yet Nvidia only focused on Huang!
"Jensen Huang is an incredible innovator. But that does not abrogate their duties of compliance.… pic.twitter.com/yYpZKOnjhF
— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) November 15, 2026
Nvidia’s Form 8-K confirms that the board accepted Huang’s resignation effective November 11 and installed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The company said its permanent search will consider both internal and external candidates.
That puts the board’s current position directly at odds with Bessent’s advice. Nvidia is leaving both doors open; Bessent says the internal door should be shut.
The filing shows that Kress will keep her CFO duties while running the company and notes that she has led Nvidia’s finance organization since 2013. The board also elevated director Harvey Jones, who has served since 1993, to become its first chair.
Nvidia told investors that operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap should continue without interruption. The leadership structure is designed to project stability, yet Bessent’s argument cuts directly against that message: if the problem was cultural rather than personal, promoting from within may preserve the very system the board is being asked to investigate.
The Associated Press reports that Singapore-based Megaspeed says it runs a lawful business and has hired outside lawyers for an internal investigation. The company said Alice Huang left in August 2025 and disputed reports about its operations, while Singapore authorities previously found insufficient evidence to charge her.
The same report says Megaspeed has faced scrutiny over allegations that advanced Nvidia chips were routed to Chinese companies. Bessent’s stated concern is whether Nvidia maintained a real culture of compliance around U.S. restrictions, regardless of the unresolved intelligence claims surrounding Alice Huang.
Singapore authorities began examining Megaspeed in February 2025 over possible false declarations tied to server purchases. They questioned Alice Huang and temporarily withheld her passport, then ultimately found insufficient evidence to charge her.
Beijing has rejected the spy allegations, and the Justice Department has not publicly reached that conclusion either.
Megaspeed says it has cooperated with U.S. Commerce Department inspections and is prepared to assist other authorities. That response matters because it draws a clean line between allegations and established facts while leaving the central compliance question alive: who knew where the chips were going, and what did Nvidia do when warning signs appeared?
Investor Michael Burry then highlighted the stakes from the market side, pointing to the allegations about China-bound chips and Nvidia’s accounting methodology.
This, NVIDIA’s changing of methodology, and Huang’s desire to get chips to China, as alleged this morning in the WSJ shows both incentives and means were in place for unsavory actions. https://t.co/ZoOUtDatys
— Cassandra Unchained (@michaeljburry) November 15, 2026
Burry’s post is one investor’s interpretation of allegations that remain unproven. Its significance is the market pressure it captures: Nvidia must now defend its controls and financial credibility while choosing a new leader.
Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results Tuesday. Kress will have to explain how the company policed restricted sales and why investors should trust the numbers she presents.
Removing Huang did not answer those questions. The board now has a Trump Cabinet secretary demanding records, outside leadership, and accountability that reaches beyond one departed executive.
This is a Guest Post from our friends over at WLTReport. View the original article here.

sources.news_title: Scott Bessent urges Nvidia to appoint an external CEO
sources.text:
WS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said Nvidia needs to "go outside the company" as it seeks a new chief executive after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week.
Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis.
"This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" show.
Bessent also said Nvidia's board and outside counsel needed to answer, within the next 10 days, questions about the company's culture of compliance with export restrictions.
Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential replacement for Huang, the Financial Times said on Friday.

sources.news_title: Bessent calls for Nvidia leadership shake-up amid China chip scandal, urges outside CEO
sources.text:
Bessent calls for Nvidia leadership shake-up amid China chip scandal, urges outside CEO
'They need a dramatic shake-up,' Treasury Secretary Bessent said
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for Nvidia to hire its next CEO from outside the company following Jensen Huang's resignation, arguing that questions surrounding the chipmaker's compliance with U.S. export restrictions warrant a major leadership shake-up on "Sunday Morning Futures."
Bessent questioned whether Nvidia's alleged export compliance failures were isolated incidents or reflected deeper problems within the company.
"We will see if Nvidia intentionally ignored the warning signs of these shell companies, many of them in Singapore," Bessent said, claiming that Nvidia's accounts showed a crash in sales to China followed by a surge in sales to Singapore.
"And I have seen reporting that only 1% of the chips sold in Singapore remained in Singapore," he added. "This makes me think that, as the board conducts a search for a new leader, that they need to go outside the company."
NVIDIA STOCK SLIDE WIPES OUT MORE THAN $20B IN VALUE FOR JENSEN HUANG OVER 5 DAYS
"They need a dramatic shake-up."
The Treasury chief's comments follow Huang's resignation Thursday after Nvidia's board investigated his reported affair with a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence source.
Huang is also alleged to have had extramarital relationships with two employees at Nvidia.
Regardless of Huang's "foibles," Bessent demanded answers "in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel."
JENSEN HUANG JOINS LIST OF HIGH-PROFILE FOUNDERS OUSTED FROM THEIR OWN COMPANIES
Nvidia's board of directors has approached Rene Haas, the CEO of British chipmaker Arm, in its search for the successor to Jensen Huang, according to a report from the Financial Times.
The outlet reported Friday that Haas, who had led Arm since 2022, spent seven years working at Nvidia more than a decade ago and has a "strong relationship" with Huang and some of Nvidia's board members.
"It’s a no comment from us," Arm told FOX Business when asked about the report.
CLICK HERE TO READ MORE ON FOX BUSINESS
In the meantime, Colette Kress, Nvidia's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, has agreed to serve as interim CEO in the wake of Huang's departure, the company said Thursday.
"The Board is initiating a search for a permanent chief executive officer and will consider internal and external candidates," Nvidia said.
FOX Business' Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Nvidia needs dramatic shake-up, Bessent demands external CEO after Huang exit
sources.text:
Nvidia needs dramatic shake-up, Bessent demands external CEO after Huang exit
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia to appoint an external chief executive and investigate its export compliance. The demands deepen scrutiny after Jensen Huang's resignation amid an alleged espionage-linked scandal.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to appoint a chief executive from outside the company, saying the chipmaker needs a “dramatic shake-up” following the resignation of Jensen Huang amid an alleged espionage-linked infidelity scandal.
Bessent also demanded an urgent investigation into Nvidia's compliance with US export restrictions, questioning whether the company's executives deliberately ignored warning signs about Singapore-based companies allegedly acting as intermediaries to supply advanced AI chips to China.
Speaking to Fox News on Sunday, Bessent said Nvidia's board should look beyond its existing leadership while searching for Huang's successor.
“They need to go outside the company. Just what was going on inside the company, they needed a dramatic shake-up,” he said.
Huang resigned on Thursday following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, and another with a senior colleague at Nvidia.
The leadership crisis has intensified scrutiny of the world's leading AI chipmaker, which plays a critical role in the global artificial intelligence industry and the US economy.
Nvidia has reportedly approached Rene Haas, chief executive of British chipmaker Arm, about taking over the role. AMD CEO Lisa Su is also being viewed as a potential external candidate. US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has suggested that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should lead Nvidia.
Among the internal contenders are interim CEO Colette Kress, who previously served as Nvidia's chief financial officer, and Ian Buck, who heads the company's data centre business.
Bessent said the company must establish whether its leadership had maintained adequate compliance standards regarding US restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.
“Was it a low-level fail? Was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? And who knew?” he asked, questioning whether Nvidia had used shell companies as a workaround to sell restricted chips to China.
He also demanded answers from Nvidia's board and external legal advisers within 10 days, warning that authorities would examine whether the company had deliberately overlooked suspicious transactions involving Singapore-based firms.
EXPORT CONTROLS UNDER SCRUTINY
Bessent has repeatedly criticised the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to block exports of Nvidia chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company allegedly linked to the Chinese intelligence asset involved in the Huang scandal.
US authorities are investigating whether Megaspeed, which builds AI data centres across Asia, was involved in smuggling advanced Nvidia chips into China.
The Treasury secretary accused the Commerce Department of delaying efforts to place Megaspeed on Washington's national security blacklist, despite concerns raised by other government departments.
“Many other departments were pushing for this, and commerce had the pen,” Bessent said. “We have all the rules we need. We just need them enforced.”
Lutnick is facing growing pressure from within the Trump administration and Congress to explain why exports to the Singaporean company were allowed to continue despite the alleged national security links.
The controversy has also accelerated efforts by US lawmakers to tighten restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China.
Comparing Nvidia's alleged compliance failures to violations in the banking sector, Bessent said that if the company were a bank, regulators would already have intervened and removed several executives.
HUANG TO TESTIFY BEFORE CONGRESS
Meanwhile, Republican Congressman John Moolenaar, chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, said Huang had agreed to testify before Congress.
Two other House committees, dealing with foreign affairs and intelligence, have also demanded that the former Nvidia chief appear before their members.
The dates for his testimony are still being negotiated, Moolenaar said.
He told CBS News that lawmakers wanted to understand whether sensitive information had been accessed and whether the alleged Chinese intelligence asset had influenced Nvidia's corporate approach to artificial intelligence and US export controls.

sources.news_title: US Treasury chief wants answers soon from Nvidia
sources.text:
US Treasury chief wants answers soon from Nvidia
San Francisco (United States) (AFP) – US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia Sunday to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged spy for Beijing.
Issued on:
Speaking on "Fox News Sunday Morning Futures" three days after Huang resigned, Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge US restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China.
The United States forbids sales to China of the most-cutting edge AI chips, hoping to stay ahead of the Chinese in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.
In late 2025, President Donald Trump did authorize sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese -- but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.
"Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese," Bessent said.
"What's more important here," he said, "is to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions."
He alluded to companies linked to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company that Huang's alleged lover Alice Huang once worked for.
"And who knew? Because I mean, these shell companies were obvious. They were being investigated. And did Nvidia use them as a workaround to sell chips to the Chinese?"
Of Alice Huang he said: "It doesn't matter to me whether she's a spy or not. You know, Jensen's foibles are his foibles."
Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang's behavior within the next 10 days.
Megaspeed is suspected by the United States of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls by buying Nvidia chips for its data centers in Southeast Asia and routing them to China.
The Justice Department is carrying out a criminal probe.
Nvidia late last month said it had investigated these allegations last year and refuted them.
The Financial Times has reported that four federal agencies pushed to have Megaspeed blacklisted by the Commerce Department run by Howard Lutnick, but the latter did not do so.
"Many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen," Bessent said, repeating remarks he made Friday that suggest fissures in the Trump administration on this issue.
Senators have summoned Jensen Huang to testify before the chamber's Banking Committee next month.
Lutnick himself has also reportedly agreed to testify.
Jensen Huang has also agreed to testify behind closed doors in the House of Representatives before Thanksgiving.
Nvidia is due to publish its quarterly results on Tuesday.

sources.news_title: Bessent Urges Nvidia Outside CEO Search
sources.text:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia to choose a CEO from outside the company, calling for a “dramatic shakeup” after Jensen Huang stepped down. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, and reports said the board had considered Arm chief Rene Haas as a potential successor. Bessent demanded that Nvidia’s board and outside lawyers respond within 10 days about the company’s compliance culture and adherence to U.S. export controls. The scrutiny centers on Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, which U.S. authorities suspect of helping divert restricted AI chips to China, as well as questions about Nvidia’s sales and disclosures. Reports linked Huang’s resignation to personal relationships, including one involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials reportedly suspect of spying for China; those suspicions have not been publicly established.

sources.news_title: Scott Bessent says Nvidia should look outside the company for a new CEO: ‘They needed a dramatic shake-up'
sources.text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has thoughts about Nvidia's search for a new CEO.
Bessent said Nvidia's board of directors should focus on candidates "outside the company" during an interview on Fox's "Sunday Morning Futures."
"They need a dramatic shake-up," Bessent said.
Last week, now former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after the company's board of directors opened an investigation into whether he was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort."
The same day, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a memo to staff. The New York Times and Reuters reported in the days following that Huang also had relationships with two different Nvidia employees.
An October New York Times report said Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, a former tech executive whom US officials believe may have been passing information to China. China has denied the espionage claims, and the US Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion on the matter.
During the interview, Bessent also said Nvidia's board of directors should answer questions about the company's compliance with export regulations in the next 10 days.
"Nvidia is a wonderful company. Jensen Huang is an incredible innovator, but that does not abrogate their duties to compliance," he said.
In a statement, Nvidia said it would consider both internal and external candidates for the CEO role. Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer, is serving as interim CEO. The board has not publicly discussed potential candidates, but some analysts and investors have shared their top picks.
Others, meanwhile, are hoping that Nvidia's board reinstates Huang as CEO until an internal investigation into his affair is complete.
There is a growing number of people in the tech industry who believe the allegations that Alice Huang is a spy might have been intentionally overblown by China hawks in the US looking to oust Huang. The former Nvidia CEO had been an advocate for supplying chips to China.

sources.news_title: Bessent says Nvidia should look outside the company new CEO after Huang: ‘Needs a dramatic shakeup’
sources.text:
Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside the company for new CEO after Jensen Huang’s resignation: ‘Dramatic shakeup’
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Nvidia should look “outside the company” to replace its CEO, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said — but it shouldn’t wait too Huang.
Founder Jensen Huang famously had no succession plan and the board must now push a “dramatic shakeup,” Bessent told Larry Kudlow Sunday on Fox News’ “Sunday Morning Futures.”
The $4 trillion firm also owes the Trump administration answers within 10 days about whether it was profiting off of banned chip sales.
“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said.
“And I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel.”
Huang, 63, resigned last week as president, CEO and director of the company, which he cofounded at a Denny’s in 1993.
His exit followed reports of an affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, as well as a married underling at the company.
“This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said. “They needed a dramatic shakeup.”
Huang admitted to the affair Nov. 8 in a staff-wide memo. Three days later, The New York Times reported that he had also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.
The board accepted his resignation that night and announced it the following morning.
CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO. Harvey Jones, a director since the company’s founding, became the company’s first-ever board chair.
Nvidia has said it will consider both internal and external candidates for the permanent replacement.
Here’s the latest on the Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy:
- Jensen Huang eyeing comeback as Nvidia CEO forming ‘war room’ with allies in wake of Chinese spy, employee affairs: report
- Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside the company for new CEO after Huang’s resignation
- ‘SNL’ roasts ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang over Chinese ‘spy’ sex scandal
- Howard Lutnick in the hot seat as lawmakers demand answers on Nvidia sales to China
The Treasury secretary has spent the week pressing a narrower question than who’s sleeping with whom: who bought Nvidia’s chips, and where they ended up.
Alice Huang was an executive for the Singapore-based, Alibaba-backed datacenter company Megaspeed, which has been accused of smuggling high-end Nvidia chips to China — despite a US ban.
“The real story here should be, did Nvidia know their client?” Bessent said Friday on CNBC. He added that anyone at the company responsible for letting chips slip through the cracks should be “held accountable.”
“We do not know for a fact that Jensen Huang knew this,” he added.
Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.
Bessent also blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s team, whose jurisdiction includes export controls.
He said Treasury, the State Department, the Defense Department and the US Trade Representative had backed blacklisting Megaspeed “for months.”
Nvidia will report quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first report without Huang at the helm.
Huang has also agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees Dec. 1, and the Senate Banking Committee has asked him to testify the same week.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said NVIDIA needs to “go outside the company” as it seeks a new chief executive after Jensen Huang stepped down amid revelations of extramarital affairs.
Bessent was speaking to Fox News’ “Sunday Morning Futures” show.
Outside candidates to replace Jensen Huang
Among the outside candidates the chipmaker’s board is reportedly considering are two Israelis: Johny Srouji, Apple’s chief hardware officer, and Eyal Waldman, founder and former CEO of Mellanox.
According to Calcalist, Srouji’s main advantage is his experience leading Apple’s silicon strategy, which allowed the iPhone maker to develop its own chips for its products. The main argument against his appointment is that he was promoted to chief hardware officer only in April 2026, a little more than half a year ago.
Waldman is also among those being considered, Ynet reported. He co-founded Mellanox, an Israeli networking company that NVIDIA acquired in 2020 for some $7 billion, and his experience as a CEO could give him an edge.
Other outside candidates reportedly being considered include Rene Haas, CEO of Arm and a former NVIDIA executive; Lisa Su, CEO of NVIDIA competitor AMD; and Matt Garman, CEO of Amazon Web Services.
Trump pushes Tim Cook as NVIDIA’s next CEO
US President Donald Trump has also weighed in, saying former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take the helm.
“NOW THAT NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump wrote on social media. “A Legend replaces a Legend!”
A third Israeli, Michael Kagan, NVIDIA’s chief technology officer, is also reportedly under consideration, according to Calcalist. Kagan co-founded Mellanox with Waldman and has spent the past several years developing technology at NVIDIA, giving him contacts inside the company.
Tobias Holcman contributed to this story.

sources.news_title: ‘Dramatic shakeup’: Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside company for Huang’s successor
Bessent Demands Nvidia Leadership Shake-Up as Huang Supporters Petition for His Return
sources.text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for a major overhaul of Nvidia’s leadership following Jensen Huang’s resignation, questioning whether the chipmaker pursued potentially illegal sales of advanced artificial intelligence processors to inflate revenue and earnings.
In an interview on Fox News on Sunday, Bessent said Nvidia’s board should look outside the company for a permanent chief executive and suggested that other executives could face scrutiny over the company’s compliance with US export controls.
“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said.

His comments add a new dimension to the crisis facing the world’s leading AI chipmaker, which is dealing with questions about its leadership, potential export-control violations and the financial relationships surrounding its business partners. The remarks also come two days before Nvidia is scheduled to release its first quarterly results since Huang’s departure.
Bessent suggested the company’s problems extended beyond its former chief executive, arguing that regulators would take a broader approach if a financial institution faced comparable compliance concerns.
“If this were a bank and they hadn’t complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed,” he said, referring to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
He also questioned Nvidia’s financial disclosures, pointing to an increase in reported Singapore revenue as sales to China declined. Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, explaining that it had adopted a new methodology based on customers’ headquarters rather than billing addresses to provide a more accurate picture of its geographical sales distribution.
The dispute is based partly on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected by US authorities of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of American export restrictions. Huang resigned on Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence officials suspect of spying for China.
Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive while its board searches for a permanent replacement.
Washington’s Export-Control Dispute Widens
Bessent’s intervention comes amid growing tensions between the Treasury Department and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department over the suspected diversion of advanced AI processors to China.
Speaking to CNBC’s “Squawk Box” on Friday, Bessent said several federal agencies had supported adding Megaspeed to the government’s export blacklist for months.
“But Commerce has the pen,” he said, referring to the department’s authority over export-control decisions.
His remarks followed an Axios report that Bessent confronted Lutnick in the White House Situation Room over Commerce’s failure to act against Megaspeed. The Commerce Department denied that the confrontation occurred.
Lutnick is facing separate scrutiny over financial relationships involving his family and Nvidia’s business partners. CNBC reported on Friday that Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm formerly run by Lutnick and now led by his sons, had helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies doing business with Nvidia.
Cantor said its Nvidia shareholdings had fallen nearly 50% over six months as national security concerns surrounding Huang intensified. The positions were linked to client swap transactions rather than proprietary investments, the firm said.
There is no evidence that Lutnick shared sensitive government information with his sons or that Cantor traded on such information.
Bessent also defended President Donald Trump’s handling of the export-control dispute, saying the president had drawn a firm line against sales to China of chips more advanced than Nvidia’s H200 processor.
Trump authorized sales of H200 chips to approved Chinese customers in December following months of lobbying by Huang. The arrangement requires the US government to receive 25% of the proceeds.
The dispute exposes competing pressures within Washington’s approach to AI technology. The administration wants to protect American leadership in advanced computing while determining how much access Chinese companies should have to US-designed processors. Allegations that restricted chips were diverted through third parties have intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s commercial relationships and the effectiveness of export enforcement.
Shareholders and Musk Push for Huang’s Return
While Bessent is demanding a leadership overhaul, a section of Nvidia’s shareholders and employees is campaigning for Huang to return as chief executive.
A petition calling for his reinstatement had attracted more than 100,000 signatures by Saturday afternoon, according to reports. The campaign, hosted on standwithjesen.com, reportedly included approximately 60,000 shareholders, 6,000 current employees and 1,000 former employees.
Among Huang’s reported supporters was Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, who warned that Nvidia could lose important commercial relationships without its co-founder.
“Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract,” Musk wrote on X on Saturday.
“Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.”
Musk’s comments point to the importance of Huang’s personal relationships in Nvidia’s business model. The company’s expansion has involved close relationships with major technology companies, cloud computing providers, and infrastructure operators. Some of those arrangements may have been built around Huang’s direct involvement and influence across the industry.
His departure therefore raises questions about whether Nvidia can preserve the commercial relationships that helped establish its dominance in AI computing under a new chief executive.
Kress, who will lead the company on an interim basis, said Nvidia would build on the foundation Huang established over more than three decades.
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” she said in the company’s announcement.
Nvidia had initially backed Huang after he acknowledged the affair, but later said it would conduct an independent investigation following reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
The company now faces an immediate test as investors prepare to assess its financial performance and the implications of the leadership transition.
Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said he saw little prospect of Huang returning, arguing that the allegations had created legal, board-level and political complications that would make reinstatement difficult.
“No one individual can replace Jensen as CEO,” Ives said, while arguing that the company’s former leadership image could not simply be restored after the scandal.
He added that the focus should shift to Nvidia’s next phase under Kress, beginning with Tuesday’s earnings announcement.
The results will be important because Nvidia remains central to the global AI investment cycle. Investors will be looking for evidence that demand for its processors remains strong and that the management transition has not disrupted customer relationships or the company’s operating plans.
However, the questions raised by Bessent introduce risks beyond the usual earnings assessment. Potential export-control violations, scrutiny of financial disclosures, and the possibility of further regulatory action could affect Nvidia’s relationships with customers and its ability to sell advanced processors into international markets.

Bessent Gives Nvidia Board 10 Days to Address Export-Control Concerns
The demand concerns allegations that Nvidia AI chips reached China through Singapore-based Megaspeed.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave Nvidia’s board 10 days on Sunday to explain potential export-control failures, putting the chipmaker’s handling of alleged China-bound chip diversions under direct federal scrutiny.
Bessent sought answers on whether advanced Nvidia AI chips reached China through Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. The concern is possible diversion through an intermediary in a third country, rather than a direct Nvidia sale to China. Bessent said potential breaches could undermine national security.
His request calls for immediate clarification from Nvidia’s directors about compliance with U.S. export controls. Bessent also criticized the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, for not acting on earlier recommendations to add Megaspeed to the U.S. Entity List.
The concern is whether Nvidia can verify where its products end up after sale. The chips are used to train large AI models, making their destination strategically significant. The board’s response is due within 10 days of Bessent’s Nov. 15 demand.

sources.news_title: Treasury Secretary Bessent gives Nvidia's board 10 days to explain export-control failures
sources.text:
Treasury Secretary Bessent gives Nvidia’s board 10 days to explain export-control failures
United States Department of the Treasury
Scott Bessent wants answers on alleged chip diversion to China through Singapore-based Megaspeed, and he is not hiding his frustration with Commerce
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has put Nvidia’s board on a clock. He wants answers within 10 days about export-control failures and the national security risks tied to them.
The demand, made on November 15, 2026, centers on allegations that advanced Nvidia AI chips were illicitly routed to China through Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore. If true, that would put some of the most tightly controlled hardware in the world in exactly the place US policy is designed to keep it out of.
What Bessent is asking for
Bessent called for immediate clarification from Nvidia’s directors on the company’s compliance with US export controls. His concern is that potential breaches could undermine national security.
Under current US policy, Nvidia cannot sell chips above the H200/H100 tier to China. Washington cites the risk of technology leakage as the reason. Those chips power the training of large AI models, which makes them strategically valuable in a way most consumer hardware is not.
The alleged problem is not that Nvidia sold banned chips directly to China. It is that chips may have reached China anyway, through an intermediary in a third country.
A side swipe at Commerce
Bessent’s remarks were not aimed solely at Nvidia. He also expressed frustration with the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick.

His complaint: Commerce did not act on earlier recommendations to add Megaspeed to the US entity list. Multiple government agencies had reportedly supported that move.
Congress has noticed. Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott has reportedly summoned Lutnick and Jensen Huang to testify about export-control enforcement. Bessent’s comments have fueled bipartisan concern on Capitol Hill, and Nvidia may face a broader investigation into its sales practices and compliance culture.
Why the timing is awkward for Nvidia
The scrutiny lands as Nvidia prepares to report its fiscal Q3 earnings. Export restrictions have shaped Nvidia’s business for years. The Megaspeed allegations raise a different concern: not what Nvidia is allowed to sell, but whether it can verify where its products end up.
What this means
For Nvidia shareholders, the near-term risk is uncertainty. Compliance failures, if confirmed, could bring restrictions on product sales and hit revenue.
The 10-day window gives the market a concrete date to watch. A detailed, credible answer from the board could ease some pressure. A vague one could invite exactly the kind of deeper investigation lawmakers are already signaling.
Bessent has effectively put Commerce on notice alongside Nvidia. Whether Lutnick’s department moves to add Megaspeed to the entity list could become an early test of how aggressively the administration plans to enforce chip export rules, and how much tolerance it has for gaps in that enforcement.
